title: Circular dependency awareness
learningObjectives: Explain circular dependency awareness and build modular, event-driven browser code.

understand.concept: A circular dependency occurs when modules depend on each other directly or through a chain. ES modules support cycles, but evaluation order and live bindings can expose uninitialized bindings or fragile design. Avoid cycles where possible by extracting shared contracts or moving responsibilities.
understand.whyItMatters: Circular dependencies make initialization harder to reason about and can cause runtime errors. Clear one-way dependency direction improves architecture.
understand.analogy: A circular dependency is like two rooms waiting for each other to finish setting up before either can open.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is simplified; module loading and DOM event behaviour follow web platform standards.

explain.narrative: A shared contract module provides common definitions without forcing the two feature modules to import each other.

examples.explanation: A shared contract module provides common definitions without forcing the two feature modules to import each other.
examples.expectedOutput: Browser console output demonstrates module or event behaviour; DOM examples require matching elements.

practise.guidedTask: Draw a dependency graph for three modules. Identify a cycle and refactor the shared contract into a lower-level module.
practise.independentTask: Build a small feature using explicit module boundaries or DOM event handling. Test keyboard, pointer, dynamic content, and failure cases as appropriate.
hints: Keep module responsibilities and public exports clear.
Preserve native keyboard and form behaviour.

questions.prompt: What is a common way to reduce circular module dependencies?
options: Extract shared contracts into a lower-level module
questions.answer: Extract shared contracts into a lower-level module
questions.explanation: A shared lower-level dependency can remove a cycle between higher-level modules.

questions.prompt: What is a good principle for modular event-driven code?
options: Use clear contracts and preserve expected browser behaviour
Stop all propagation for every event
Expose every internal module binding globally
questions.answer: Use clear contracts and preserve expected browser behaviour
questions.explanation: Explicit interfaces and predictable event handling reduce coupling and preserve usability.
